To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the monomeric and dimeric forms of E. coli Thymidine Kinase are both very sensitive to u.v. radiation, but dimeric thymidine kinase is more sensitive.

the catalytic activity, the dCDP binding site and the dTTP binding site of thymidine dimeric forms of E. coli Thymidine Kinase are more resistant to u.v. radiation than the corresponding monomeric forms.

the monomeric form of thymidine kinases is more sensitive to u.v. radiation than the dimeric form, that dCDP and dTTP protect the monomeric but not the dimeric enzyme, and that the protection afforded to the monomeric enzyme by dCDP and ATP is additive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of small molecules on u.v. sensitivity of monomeric and dimeric forms of thymidine Kinase.
the effects of small molecules, both substrates and allosteric regulators, on the u.v. sensitivity of the catalytic activities of E. coli deoxythymidine kinase.
the following questions: (1) Does the catalytic site of thymidine kinases from E. coli and other organisms contain residues that are particularly sensitive to U.V. damage?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects observed are consistent with the view that dTTP and dCDP alter enzyme conformation in such a way as to protect the catalytic site of the enzyme from u.v.-induced damage.
the effects of allosteric effectors of E. coli Thymidine kinase on its u.v.sensitivity are due to an alteration in the conformation of the protein.
, the effects of dCDP and dTTP are similar to that of ATP and thymidin, and are not due to the absorption of energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catalytic activity is more sensitive to u.v. radiation than the regulatory activity.
dCDP and dTTP protect against u.v. inactivation of thymidine kinases in the monomeric and dimeric forms.
the dCDP and dTTP are not protecting agents for thymidine kinase and that the protection afforded by ATP and thymine is due to complex formation with the catalytic subunit of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dimeric form of thymidine kinases is more sensitive to UV irradiation than the monomeric form.
dCDP, dGTP and dTTP protect the catalytic activity from u.v. radiation.
dCDP, which is a negative effector of the catalytic site of the enzyme, protects the catalytic activity from inactivation by u.v. radiation.
